validation.spec_summary: The Defender Clone project delivers a browser‑based arcade shooter reminiscent of the classic 1981 Defender game. The stack consists of a Python 3.11+ FastAPI backend (served by Uvicorn) and a vanilla JavaScript/HTML5 Canvas frontend. All source code lives under the `defender/` directory. The backend provides three routes: a root GET that serves the HTML shell, a static file handler for the frontend assets, and a pair of `/score` endpoints that store a per‑session high score in memory. The frontend implements a full game loop with a scrolling world, player ship, enemies, humanoids, bullets, HUD and minimap. Controls are keyboard‑only (A/D or arrows, W/S, Space, Enter, P, Escape). Scoring follows a detailed table, and the high score can be posted to the backend. The implementation must be fully functional – no placeholder stubs. Unit tests are written with pytest and use FastAPI’s TestClient to verify static serving, score handling, and high‑score logic. The test suite is run with `cd defender/backend && pytest -q`. The README explains how to install dependencies (`pip install -r backend/requirements.txt`), start the server (`uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload`), and play the game. The project is split into five delivery phases: backend implementation, static HTML/CSS, core JavaScript game modules, the main orchestration script, and documentation. Each phase has a targeted QA command that validates the presence and basic correctness of its files before moving on. The final deliverable is a playable game that runs at 60 fps, with all backend tests passing and no stub files remaining.
